statement: We are modeling the pore space of a granular material (lunar regolith) in which water ice sublimates and deposits. Treat the pore space as a three-dimensional region filled with solid ice and gas. The local volume fraction of ice is the phase field phi(x, y, z, t), between 0 and 1: phi = 1 in ice and phi = 0 in gas, with a thin, smooth transition between the two. Construct the free energy of this system as a functional of the phase field, F[phi] = integral of f over the volume, at phase coexistence (constant temperature, no driving force for growth or sublimation). It must make bulk ice and bulk gas the stable states, and give an interface between them that has a finite width and an energy per unit area. Choose the form of f, and write its coefficients in terms of gamma and eps only (and numbers), so that a flat interface at equilibrium has energy per unit area exactly gamma and a width proportional to eps; say what multiple of eps the width is, and how you define the width. Explain why each term is there. State every assumption, and list every effect you leave out with the reason. Return the free energy density f.

symbols.name: phi(x, y, z, t)
symbols.meaning: local volume fraction of ice (phase field), between 0 and 1

symbols.name: gamma
symbols.meaning: energy per unit area of the ice-gas interface, constant

symbols.name: eps
symbols.meaning: a length that sets the width of the diffuse interface, constant

assumptions: the temperature is uniform and constant, at phase coexistence

deliverable.notes: f is an energy per unit volume. Write it with phi(x, y, z, t) and its first derivatives only, for example Derivative(phi(x, y, z, t), x); no second derivatives. Use only these names, numbers, + - * / ** and parentheses. Your symbols list may stay empty if f needs no other names.
